How to Pass Front-End I

UDIT 2026-27 · Grado en Desarrollo Full-Stack / Data-Science & AI

Rubén Vega Balbás, PhD · ruvebal@crea-comm.net

6 ECTS · 150h total · 30h laboratory · Annual

Course Information

Academic Year2026-27
SemesterAnnual (both semesters)
ECTS6
InstructorRubén Vega Balbás, PhD
Emailruvebal@crea-comm.net

This document details the deliverables, evaluation tests, and requirements to successfully complete Front-End I. Delivery dates may vary from the indicative dates shown here.

Evaluation Structure

ComponentWeight
Pruebas (Tests)30%
Trabajos, entregables y proyectos (Projects)60%
Portafolio (Problem-solving portfolio)10%

Total: 100% · Pass threshold: 5.0 average

Deliverable 1: Portfolio Template

NamePortfolio Template (Semester 1)
DescriptionThree-level progressive implementation: vanilla → Bootstrap+GSAP → Tailwind+Vite
Indicative DateEnd of Semester 1 (January 2027)
% Evaluation25%
RequirementsComplete all three grade levels with GitHub deployment

Deliverable 2: Geophysical Aggregator

NameGeophysical Aggregator Project (Semester 2)
DescriptionIndividual React Router v7 Framework Mode app with public APIs, i18n, auth, deployment
Indicative DateWeek 14-15 (May 2027)
% Evaluation30%
RequirementsComplete all mandatory requirements: React Query, two APIs, bilingual UI, httpOnly auth

Deliverable 3: Final Presentation

NameFinal Presentation & Monograph
DescriptionLive demo of Geophysical Aggregator + technical presentation + reflective monograph
Indicative DateFinal exam period (June 2027)
% Evaluation5%
RequirementsPresent working application with documentation and reflection

Test 1: Mid-Term Examination

NameMid-Term Written Test
DescriptionTheory and practical skills covering Semester 1 (HTML/CSS/JS fundamentals)
Indicative DateMid-Semester 1 (November 2026)
% Evaluation15%
RequirementsNo prerequisite · Covers sessions S1-S10

Test 2: Final Examination

NameFinal Written Test
DescriptionTheory and practical skills covering full annual curriculum (React focus)
Indicative DateFinal exam period (June 2027)
% Evaluation15%
RequirementsMust present Deliverables 1, 2, and 3 previously

Portfolio Component

NameProblem-Solving Portfolio
DescriptionResolution of exercises, problem-solving evidence, and session reflections
Indicative DateContinuous throughout the year
% Evaluation10%
RequirementsCommit evidence per session with ATELIER reflections

Ordinary Evaluation Criteria

  • The average of all evaluated components must reach 5.0 for the subject to be considered approved.
  • If any deliverable or test scores below 4.5, the subject will be suspended, and the student must present to the extraordinary evaluation.
  • All components must be completed to calculate the final average.

Extraordinary Evaluation

  • Students who fail the ordinary evaluation may present to the extraordinary evaluation.
  • Conditions: Must complete failed deliverables (1, 2, or 3) and/or retake failed tests (mid-term, final).
  • Type of test: Written examination covering failed content areas.
  • Portfolio evidence may be requested for review.

Important Notes

  • AI Disclosure: All AI-assisted work must follow the docs-first methodology with documented plans and implementation reports. See AI Use Declaration Rubric.
  • Oral Defence: Final presentation includes diff walkthrough and Q&A. See Oral Defence Rubric.
  • Code Quality: Projects must include linting, formatting, and follow professional standards.
  • Accessibility: WCAG 2.2 AA compliance is required for all projects.
  • Deployment: All projects must be publicly deployed with working URLs.

Key Dates Summary

  • November 2026: Mid-Term Test (15%)
  • January 2027: Portfolio Template Deliverable (25%)
  • May 2027: Geophysical Aggregator Deliverable (30%)
  • June 2027: Final Test (15%) + Final Presentation (5%)
  • Continuous: Problem-Solving Portfolio (10%)
